absent: Full encoding and width assignments for control fields beyond the validation categories shown.
Physical address derivation and lifetime rules for control structures.
Complete layout and all flags of the per processor assist page and enlightened structures.
Locking and concurrency rules for nested state beyond the shadow accessor assertion.
Detailed semantics of clean field tracking and MSR bitmap recomputation.
Exact numeric values for revision markers, sentinel addresses, timer rates, and list limits.
Behavior of direct hypercall and nested flush beyond flag propagation.
Guest visible effects and recovery after triple fault request.

findings.text: Loading a virtual control structure resolves its physical location and then selects between an enlightened path and a hardware instruction path according to a global enlightenment flag. The hardware path executes a privileged load with separate handling for logical errors and for faults.

When enlightened operation is available, the load obtains the calling processor assist page and requires it to be present, propagating a direct hypercall allowance only if the current enlightened structure advertises nested flush support, then records the supplied address as current and requests enlightened entry. When the feature is compiled out, the same operation has no effect.

Privileged virtualization instructions issued through the shared wrapper distinguish two outcomes. A fault during execution is treated as spurious and handled centrally, while a normal error indication transfers to a per instruction error routine executed with instrumentation markers around it. Successful execution simply returns to the caller.

Teardown of nested mappings releases the access page mapping, the virtual APIC mapping, and the posted descriptor mapping, and clears the cached descriptor reference so later use cannot observe a stale pointer.

Cached shadow state is written back to guest memory only when the guest controls enable the shadow feature and the link reference is valid. If the cached translation does not match the current link, it is refreshed first and the update is skipped when refresh fails. Otherwise the full cached image is stored through the cached translation.
Retrieval of the cached shadow image requires the associated virtual processor to be locked by the caller, or to be in an unreachable state, as enforced by an assertion at entry.

Secondary feature checks share a common rule that the primary activation control must be set together with the queried secondary bit. The preemption timer check instead examines the pin based controls directly.

After migration where the enlightened pointer is left in a pending state, entry processing attempts to revalidate the pointer when the guest is entitled to the feature. Failure prevents further progress, while success records that control state must later be copied from the authoritative version into the shadow copy.

Enlightened operation is considered available to a guest only when Hyper-V enlightenment is active for that virtual processor and userspace has explicitly enabled the enlightened control flag for the nested state.

Enlightened pointer handling starts disabled when the feature is unavailable or the supplied reference is invalid, releasing any prior mapping. A changed address discards the previous current marker, releases, then maps the new location and validates its revision marker, zeroing the control area on the launch path. Launch and address change both clear clean tracking and request recomputation of the MSR bitmap.

Releasing enlightened state unmaps the current region, clears the cached address and pointer, marks the stored reference invalid, and resets nested Hyper-V identity values for assist page, domain, and processor.

On nested exit the implementation copies guest register and control state from the active hardware structure into the nested control area. Always synchronized portions include control registers derived through ownership rules, stack and instruction pointers, flags, selected segment attributes, interruptibility, activity derived from processor state, and fault address. Additional portions are conditional on exit controls, paging mode, and feature enablement, including preemption timer, page table root with related entries, interrupt status, mode bit merging, debug and extended feature state, and protection state.

Guest views of control registers are composed from three sources. Bits owned by the guest come from hardware, bits masked for host ownership come from the nested control area, and remaining bits come from the read shadow. Separate ownership and mask sets apply to each of the two registers.

The remaining preemption interval is derived from the outstanding timer duration converted to nanoseconds, scaled by the virtual processor frequency into cycles, then reduced by the emulated rate factor. Expired or nonpositive remaining time yields zero.

A rarely changed subset covering segment state, descriptor table state, and pending debug state is synchronized separately and clears a deferred flag when completed. The main synchronization either performs this subset immediately when the enlightened reference is valid or arms the deferred flag otherwise.

Control flow protection state is read only when the guest advertises the relevant capabilities. One component requires either of two features, while the other components require the shadow stack feature specifically.

Reads of control fields first validate the requested encoding width, then select between an enlightened memory lookup and a hardware read based on the global enlightenment flag. An unknown enlightened offset or a build without enlightenment support yields zero rather than faulting. Narrow builds assemble wide results from paired halves.
Accessor width checks reject mismatched field encodings at build time when the field number is constant, distinguishing narrow, full, wide, high half, and natural width categories.

Exit information recording always stores reason and qualification, merging an enclave mode indication when present. If the exit reflects failed entry, no further fields change and the structure is not marked launched. Otherwise the structure is marked launched, the pending entry event validity is cleared, the injected event is transferred to vectoring state, exit details and instruction metadata are stored, and guest MSR state is saved with abort on failure.
A nested abort does not attempt recovery of guest state. It requests a triple fault for the virtual processor and emits a rate limited diagnostic carrying the supplied indicator.

Saving guest MSRs on exit walks a caller supplied list bounded by a limit derived from the misc control pair. Each entry is read from guest memory, validated, resolved to a value with a special fast path for the timestamp counter when autostore is active, then written back to the value slot of the same guest entry. Any validation, read, resolution, or write failure aborts the whole walk with an invalid argument result.

Common MSR list validation rejects accesses in the extended APIC range while that mode is enabled, rejects microcode update interfaces, and rejects nonzero reserved fields. The store path additionally rejects the system management base address because that mode is unsupported.

Observed nested state retains mappings and cached pointers for access, virtual APIC, posted descriptor, enlightened control, and shadow translation, plus markers for current pointer, pending versus invalid references, clean tracking, bitmap recomputation, deferred rare synchronization, shadow sync need, autostore slot, misc controls, and a preemption timer. The assist page carries nested control flags, current address, and entry enablement.

Several conditions silently skip work or force failure. A missing assist page triggers a bug check and aborts the load. An unsupported enlightened revision causes a VM fail result after releasing the mapping. An oversized MSR list is rejected once the derived limit is reached. Failed entry leaves most exit fields untouched, so consumers must not assume they were refreshed.

Distinct sentinel references distinguish an invalid enlightened pointer from one awaiting remap after migration, and from a valid guest address. The pending marker drives revalidation on next entry, while the invalid marker means no mapping is present.

Revision validation for the enlightened region accepts two named markers as equivalent, the current enlightened version and the legacy control revision, the latter retained for compatibility with hosts that supply the legacy value.
